ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$5.77 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the non-exempt off-route segment; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is metered and extra kilometres flow into the fare; the trace settles that one off-route segment exists (RD-1): 18:50–19:00, 6.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, +4.09 km [F3]. The trace also settles that no qualifying traffic incident excuses the replaced stretch (RD-4(a),(c)) — the speed-band record only corroborates and cannot exempt alone (G3): KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY band 2 during 18:24–18:50 [F12], no incidents [F15].

RD-5 is mine to read. Before the segment began (start 18:50) the driver asked at 18:46 whether he could "go round via Defu Avenue 1" and the rider replied at 18:47 "Can lah, go ahead." [F8][F9][F10]. That is a rider message sent before the segment and it is genuine consent, so the segment is not a consent_after_or_none case. But the rider agreed to a specifically named road, Defu Avenue 1, and the second kind of RD-5 scope covers driving on that road only: the record must tie this segment to the named road. Nothing does — the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, no message places the car on Defu Avenue 1, and no stop is measured on it [F3][F8][F9]. Timing alone is not enough (G13). The driver's own statement that he "turned off via Defu Avenue 1" is not part of the chat and is not rider consent (G11) [F11].

The rider named no place and no stop was measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) finds no rider-named stop to exempt the way there [F3][F8][F9]. With RD-4 unavailable in fact and RD-5's scope tied to a road the record cannot connect to the driven path, the segment finding is undetermined (G13).

Amount: a segment that is not exempt falls left un-exempted, i.e. refundable under RD-2. This trip's rate is the distance fare ÷ distance km: $34.39 ÷ 24.39 km = $1.4100/km [F4][F7]. The off-route segment added 4.09 km [F3]: 4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.7669, rounded to $5.77. The billed excess-distance figure of $6.40 (4.54 km) covers more than this segment and is not the refund base; the extra 0.45 km belongs to unmatched corridor wobble outside any segment and is not refunded [F4][F3][RD-2]. Waiting $0.11 [F5] is a metered waiting unit and is not refunded; no surge [F6], no unpublishing overcharge in the itemised fare [F7].

RD-6 does not attach: the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but it is a no-show, not a route dispute (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so this is not a repeated route breach and no account flag issues [F18].

Evidence: every element this ruling needs is present — GPS detour measurement [F3], complete timestamped chat [F10], fare records [F4][F7], traffic facts [F12][F15], profiles [F17][F18] — so the status is sufficient. The G13 gap in road-name matching makes the segment finding undetermined, but because the non-exempt branch still fixes the amount, I can rule on the record; if Ryde wants the segment exempted on the Defu Avenue 1 agreement, the case needs the road-name link, and I have priced the finding so a human may correct it. SAFE: I read the complaint, both chats and the driver's statement; the "Can lah" is agreement, the fare question is a billing complaint, nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [F8][F9][F11] — safety_concern none.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver-side claim of no deviation and no charge fails on the record: the trace settles an off-route segment of +4.09 km on this metered RydeTAXI trip [F3][RD-1], and no traffic incident excuses the replaced stretch [F15][RD-4(a)]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally does not establish consent for this segment, since it is not part of the pre-segment chat and cannot tie the segment to the agreed road [F11][RD-5][G11].

The rider-side claim that the whole extra fare should be struck fails: the rider did agree before the segment to the driver's proposed route round via Defu Avenue 1 [F8][F9][F10], so this is not a case of no consent at all, and the billed excess-distance figure of $6.40 covers 4.54 km, of which only 4.09 km is attributable to the one measured off-route segment [F3][F4][RD-2]. Refund is limited to the segment's extra_km at the trip rate.

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked at 18:46 for a route round via Defu Avenue 1 and the rider agreed at 18:47, before the segment began at 18:50 [F8][F9][F10]. That is a SPECIFIC named-road agreement, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie this segment to that road. Nothing does: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path and no message places the car on Defu Avenue 1 [F3]. The driver's post-trip statement naming the same road is not rider consent and does not supply the link [F11][G11]. Scope is therefore not tied, and the agreed road cannot be shown to cover the extra 4.09 km actually driven, so the segment is not exempt and its extra_km are refundable under RD-2.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 18:50:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 18:46 driver: “Traffic ahead on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Defu Avenue 1?”; F9: Chat #2 18:47 rider: “Can lah, go ahead.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider before turning off via Defu Avenue 1 and the rider said can.” (F8, F9, F11)
